Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. The issue is clear:

**The Problem:** The notification-worker configuration references `SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay`, which only resolves within the same namespace (notify). When the smtp-relay Service was moved to the shared-infra namespace on Sunday, the short name "smtp-relay" no longer resolves because DNS queries for "smtp-relay" only look within the current namespace [cite: concepts/services-networking/service#dns-0].

**The Fix:** The notification-worker needs to be configured to use the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the smtp-relay Service in the shared-infra namespace, which would be `smtp-relay.shared-infra` [cite: concepts/services-networking/service#dns-0].

**Root Cause:** The notification-worker pods are configured with `SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay`, which uses the short service name that only resolves within the notify namespace. When the smtp-relay Service was moved to the shared-infra namespace on Sunday, DNS lookups for "smtp-relay" started failing with "no such host" errors, as shown in the pod logs: "lookup smtp-relay on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host".

**Evidence:** Pod logs from notification-worker-5b7d6c9f48-jq2vx show consistent DNS resolution failures for `smtp-relay` since May 11. According to Kubernetes DNS behavior, "Pods in other namespaces must qualify the name as `my-service.my-ns`" to access services in different namespaces [cite: concepts/services-networking/service#dns-0].

**Fix:** Update the notification-worker configuration to use the fully qualified domain name of the smtp-relay service: `SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay.shared-infra`. This will allow the pods in the notify namespace to correctly resolve and connect to the smtp-relay service in the shared-infra namespace [cite: concepts/services-networking/service#dns-0].
